item.text:
Bounded to 9 web calls and stopped there. I did not inspect repository materials, so I did not invent repo-specific question IDs; I used broad fit labels instead.

**2024 Events**

| Type | Accepted claim | Source | Question IDs / fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event | Claudia Sheinbaum’s June 2024 landslide result shows Morena/AMLO’s governing coalition retained strong public support as AMLO’s term ended. | [Conoce los resultados del Conteo Rápido de la Presidencia de la República](https://centralelectoral.ine.mx/2024/06/06/conoce-los-resultados-del-conteo-rapido-de-la-presidencia-de-la-republica/) — Instituto Nacional Electoral — June 6, 2024 | Not mapped here; legitimacy, continuity, electoral support |
| Event | AMLO’s 1 September 2024 Sixth Report was a self-portrait of the term’s close, claiming gains on poverty, inflation, debt, investment, and public programs. | [Sexto informe](https://www.gob.mx/amlo/documentos/sexto-informe-376444) — Presidencia de la República 2018-2024 / Gobierno de México — September 1, 2024 | Not mapped here; executive performance, socio-economic outcomes |
| Event | The January 2024 security picture remained weak: Reuters reported extortion was far higher than when AMLO took office, making it a major risk to the economy. | [Rampant extortion reveals 'corrosive' hole in Mexico security strategy](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rampant-extortion-reveals-corrosive-hole-in-mexico-security-strategy-3283251) — Reuters via Investing.com — January 25, 2024 | Not mapped here; internal security, public order, effectiveness |

| Background | Amnesty reported in March 2024 that journalists under the federal protection mechanism were still being killed, showing the mechanism had not adequately protected high-risk media workers. | [Mexico: Killings of journalists under state protection show urgent need to strengthen federal mechanism](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/) — Amnesty International / CPJ — March 6, 2024 | Not mapped here; rights, media freedom, protection of critics |
| Background | Reuters Institute’s June 2024 Mexico overview described AMLO’s final year as one marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, human rights advocates, and the media. | [Mexico](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico) — Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism — June 17, 2024 | Not mapped here; civil liberties, media environment, polarization |
| Background | Human Rights Watch warned in August 2024 that AMLO’s proposed constitutional changes could weaken judicial independence, expand military power, and erode privacy/transparency safeguards. | [Mexico: Proposed Constitutional Changes Threaten Rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights) — Human Rights Watch — August 30, 2024 | Not mapped here; rule of law, checks and balances, rights protection |
| Background | Reuters covered the judiciary reform as deeply contested, noting protests and criticism that it could weaken independence and investor confidence. | [Mexican lower house approves controversial judicial reform](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexican-lower-house-approves-controversial-judicial-reform-3600068) — Reuters via Investing.com — September 4, 2024 | Not mapped here; judicial independence, governance quality, elite conflict |

**Bottom line**

- The strongest favorable 2024 evidence is AMLO’s coalition’s electoral success, the government’s own final report, and the late-year passage of major constitutional reforms.
- The strongest critical evidence is the persistent security problem, sustained pressure on journalists and rights defenders, and broad domestic/international concern that the judicial reform weakened institutional checks.
- The picture for 2024 is therefore mixed: politically strong and institutionally aggressive, but still facing serious security and rights criticisms.
